title: Accordion
description: A small accordion-fold book lying shut on a warm white table. Pull its edge and it rises onto its spine and lets go of its panels one crease at a time, standing up as a long zig-zag strip that carries one continuous street, printed along the top and, upside down, along the bottom for the other side. Each crease is a hinge with a little stiffness, so panels settle rather than snap, and each face catches the light at its own angle. Push it back and it folds shut.
intent: After Ed Ruscha, Every Building on the Sunset Strip (1966), https://www.moma.org/collection/works/146931: a deadpan continuous street survey that is also a great object.
